Now your question.\n\n**The loop's weakness today:** Stages can be skipped, produce hollow artifacts, or fail silently. The loop doesn't break. That's how a RISE can approve a HOLLOW RRL — the loop has no teeth.\n\n**The fix: A deterministic checkpoint chain.**\n\nEvery stage writes one thing — an SCS checkpoint record. The schema is minimal:\n\n```\nSCS-{stage}-{run}.json\n{\n  stage: 1-7,\n  name: \"RISE\",\n  result: PASS | FAIL | PARTIAL,\n  audits: \"DEATH (stage 7)\",\n  audit_verdict: \"PASS\" | \"FAIL\" | \"DISCREPANCY\",\n  artifact: \"path/to/primary/output\",\n  previous_hash: \"SHA256 of prior checkpoint\",\n  own_hash: \"SHA256 of this record\",\n  next_ready: true | false\n}\n```\n\n**The enforcement is dead simple:**\n\n1. **RISE** — reads prior DEATH's checkpoint, verifies its hash, checks all 6 prior stages had PASS. If not, session is degraded before it starts.\n\n2. **SCOUT** — reads RISE's checkpoint. Verifies fidelity map was honest (not like the false RRL approval). If RISE was dishonest, scout flags it in its own checkpoint and marks previous_stage_hash as FAIL.
